A transcript-level table has many more significant features than a gene-level one, and most functional annotations are defined on genes.
This article runs gene set enrichment on the transcript-level results, separately for protein coding transcripts and for the unproductive transcript types, so that a pathway enriched only in unproductive isoforms stands out.

It starts from the object built in the [introduction](isoformic-introduction.html):

```{r}
#| message: false
library(isoformic)
library(dplyr)

extdata <- fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata")
annot_dir <- prepare_isoformic_annotation(download_reference(version = "33", file_type = "gff"))
iso <- IsoformicExperiment(
  experiment_name = "preeclampsia_placenta",
  annot_path = annot_dir,
  assays = list(abundance = read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_abundance.parquet"))),
  col_data = read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_col_data.parquet"))
)
de_tx(iso) <- read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_det.parquet"))
de_gene(iso) <- read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_deg.parquet"))
```

## Gene sets

`read_gmt()` reads a GMT file into a named list of gene symbols; the package bundles a subset of the Reactome collection of MSigDB.

```{r}
genesets <- read_gmt(fs::path(extdata, "c2.cp.reactome.v2023.1.Hs.symbols.gmt.txt"))
length(genesets)
head(names(genesets))
```

## Enrichment per transcript category

`run_enrichment()` expands gene sets to all transcripts of their genes and runs gene set enrichment analysis (`fgsea`) separately for protein coding transcripts and for the *unproductive* categories (retained intron, nonsense-mediated decay and transcripts without a defined coding sequence), both combined and individually.
The result can be stored in the object so that it is saved with it.

```{r}
#| warning: false
set.seed(42)
enrichment <- run_enrichment(iso, genesets, pval_cutoff = 0.05)
iso@gsea$reactome <- enrichment
table(enrichment$experiment)
head(enrichment)
```

`plot_enrichment()` draws the pathways side by side for each transcript category.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 10
plot_enrichment(enrichment, n = 30, experiments = c("protein_coding", "unproductive"), nes_cutoff = 1.5)
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 10
plot_enrichment(enrichment, n = 20, experiments = c("retained_intron", "nonsense_mediated_decay", "processed_transcript"), nes_cutoff = 1.5)
```

## Enrichment on the productive fraction

Ranking genes by the change in their productive fraction rather than by fold-change targets regulated unproductive splicing; `run_productivity_enrichment()` is described in the [productivity article](isoformic-productivity.html).
